sermon.title: The Poor Will Always Be With Us 09/30/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer explains Jesus’ words that the poor will always be with us, contrasts absolute and relative poverty, and shows from Deuteronomy, Proverbs and Joshua that obeying God’s laws—diligence, planning, knowledge, sexual purity and a job skill—leads out of poverty, with stories from his own childhood and missions.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Statistics (STDs, teen parents, middle-class outcomes, Brookings) are kept as spoken and were not checked.

Poverty and shame will come to him who disdains correction, But he who regards a rebuke will be honored.
In all labor there is profit, But idle chatter leads only to poverty.

chunks.section_question: What does “where no oxen are, the crib is clean” teach?
